newsitem.title: USA: CBOT delivery focus on light wheat, heavy soyoil.
newsitem.headline: CBOT delivery focus on light wheat, heavy soyoil.

text.p: Traders early Friday said the focus in the Chicago Board of Trade delivery market was on the light amount of wheat posted and heavier-than-expected postings of soyoil.
"It just shows there is demand for the wheat in deliverable position," a trader said.

Friday was first notice day for deliveries on CBOT September contracts. Only 500,000 bushels of wheat were posted, well below expectations for 2.0 to 5.0 million bushels. Cargill Investor Services put out the wheat and chief stopper was Credit Agricole, receiving for a customer.

Traders said Credit Agricole surfaced as a "new stopper" in the delivery market. "It's a French coop but it's dangerous to say the customer is a cash account, but you can assume that's so," a trader said.
Traders said there likely will be a significant amount of short covering in the September CBOT contract Friday due to the light deliveries.
"The number (delivery) was much less than expected. Some were expecting four million," a trader said.
Traders also cited the heavy amount of soyoil posted for delivery at 3,075 lots, well above expectations for 1,000 to 2,000 lots.
The bulk of the soyoil, 1,784 lots, was put out by ADM Investor Services. Stoppers were numerous indicating weak demand for soyoil stocks.
There was no soymeal or corn posted for delivery. Soybean deliveries totalled 40,000 bushels, which is what the market was expecting, traders said.
